nodes.summary: There exist a class $\mathfrak{X}$ of groups that is a Fitting class and all of whose finite members are supersoluble, a finite group $G \in \mathfrak{X}$, and a minimal normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ that is not contained in the center of $G$.
nodes.title: A Fitting class of supersoluble groups with a non-central minimal normal subgroup

nodes.summary: The proposition that for every class $\mathfrak{X}$ of groups that is a Fitting class and all of whose finite members are supersoluble, every minimal normal subgroup of every finite group $G \in \mathfrak{X}$ is contained in the center of $G$.
nodes.title: Heineken's question on Fitting classes of supersoluble groups

nodes.summary: A class of groups is a property of groups (in the lowest type universe) that is closed under isomorphism: whenever a group $H$ has the property and $H$ is isomorphic to a group $K$, then $K$ has the property. Only the finite members of a class are used in Kourovka Problem 12.91.
nodes.title: Isomorphism-closed classes of groups (Kourovka 12.91)

nodes.summary: A class $\mathfrak{X}$ of groups is a Fitting class (of finite groups) if, for every finite group $G$: whenever $G \in \mathfrak{X}$, every normal subgroup of $G$ belongs to $\mathfrak{X}$; and whenever $N_1$ and $N_2$ are normal subgroups of $G$ that belong to $\mathfrak{X}$, the subgroup $N_1 N_2$ they generate belongs to $\mathfrak{X}$.
nodes.title: Fitting classes (Kourovka 12.91)

nodes.summary: A subgroup $N$ of a group $G$ is minimal normal if $N$ is a nontrivial normal subgroup of $G$ and every nontrivial normal subgroup $M$ of $G$ with $M \le N$ equals $N$.
nodes.title: Minimal normal subgroups (Kourovka 12.91)

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is supersoluble if it has a chain of subgroups $1 = G_0 \le G_1 \le \cdots \le G_k = G$, each normal in $G$, such that for every $i < k$ there is an element $x \in G_{i+1}$ with $G_{i+1} = \langle x \rangle G_i$; that is, every factor $G_{i+1}/G_i$ is cyclic.
nodes.title: Supersoluble groups (Kourovka 12.91)
